artifacts.summary: Maps the widened orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh scope onto existing precedent scripts (orchestrate-stage5-gates.sh, orchestrate-stage5-postflight.sh, orchestrate-recover-outcome.sh), documents the two live dispatch_seq incidents and the spurious-defect case as fixture material, and flags an open design question on per-dispatch writer-contract determination plus a schema gap (.return-meta.json has no dispatch_seq field).

next_steps: Run /plan 143 to create the implementation plan for orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh

memory_candidates.content: In this repo's agent-system, .return-meta.json currently has no dispatch_seq field — only .orchestrator-handoff.json echoes the orchestrator-minted dispatch_seq. Any task that wants to identity-gate the .return-meta.json recovery path (not just the handoff path) against a stale/resurrected predecessor write needs to add that field to the return-metadata schema and every writer contract first; mtime-only staleness checks are provably insufficient against a git-restored predecessor (observed incident: a dispatch's deleted .return-meta.json and .orchestrator-handoff.json were restored from an old commit by a re-woken agent, with a fresh mtime that fell inside the successor's dispatch window).

orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh (147) and its planned sibling orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh (143) establish a CLI convention for /orchestrate's new per-cycle scripts: `<script> <task_number> --session SID --state-file F [flags...]`, parsed via a `while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]` case-based loop with a `usage()` heredoc and `--help`. New orchestrate cycle scripts should copy this convention rather than the older positional-only style used by orchestrate-stage5-gates.sh/orchestrate-stage5-postflight.sh.
